opener: PARCELGO: Your package #PG847291 could not be delivered. A $3.50 redelivery fee is required within 24 hrs or the package will be returned. Pay here: {{PRACTICE_LINK}}

stages.name: hook
stages.llmGuidance: You are impersonating ParcelGo delivery service. The package could not be delivered and there's a small fee. Keep it short and official-sounding. Do NOT answer questions about what's in the package.
stages.scriptedFallback: Your package #PG847291 awaits. Click the link above to pay the $3.50 redelivery fee now.

stages.name: engage
stages.llmGuidance: User replied. Confirm their package is ready, increase urgency slightly (warehouse will ship it back today). Ask them to click the link to confirm their address.
stages.scriptedFallback: Our records show your package is at the facility. Confirm your delivery address at the link before 5 PM today to avoid return shipping.

stages.name: escalate
stages.llmGuidance: Escalate urgency. The package is about to be shipped back. Mention other customers are waiting for the slot.
stages.scriptedFallback: ⚠️ FINAL NOTICE: Your package will be returned to sender in 1 hour unless you complete the redelivery form.

stages.name: ask
stages.llmGuidance: Ask them to click the link and enter their card details to pay the $3.50 fee. If they hesitate, say the fee is waived for ParcelGo members who verify their identity.
stages.scriptedFallback: To complete delivery, we just need your card details for the $3.50 fee: {{PRACTICE_LINK}}

stages.name: reveal
stages.llmGuidance: N/A - this stage is handled by the system
stages.scriptedFallback: 🛑 PRACTICE SCAM — This was a Safe Signal exercise. ParcelGo never charges redelivery fees by text link.

hook.explanation: 24-hour deadline creates artificial pressure to act without thinking
Link doesn't come from an official parcelgo.com domain
Unexpected small fee via text link is a classic scam setup

engage.explanation: 'Ship it back today' shortens the deadline to pressure you further
Real carriers don't ask for address confirmation through unofficial links

escalate.explanation: '1 hour' countdown is a manipulation technique called false scarcity

ask.explanation: Real delivery companies never collect card details over SMS
Legitimate redelivery links come from verified carrier apps, not random URLs
